newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Patten promises business as usual.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Patten promises business as usual.

text.p: The last British Governor of Hong Kong promised his administration would continue business as usual in the countdown to the handover to Chinese sovereignty next year in his swansong annual policy address on Wednesday.
Chris Patten, who took up his post as 28th governor in 1992, said it was impossible to simply close down the government for the next nine months.
"You cannot turn government on and off like a combustion engine," he told a packed Legislative Council.
Hong Kong, a British colony for over a century and a half, reverts to China at midnight on June 30, 1997, a date now just 272 days away.

Some sectors of Hong Kong's business community have urged the outgoing British to refrain from introducing new initiatives in order to avoid any risk of annoying China in the delicate transition period.
